asDecan.p: Every sign is cut into three slices of ten degrees, called decans, and each slice has a ruling planet and a small card of its own. Your Sun sits somewhere between 10 and 19 degrees of Virgo, the middle of the sign, where Virgo has settled in and is at full strength, and the planet in charge of that slice is Venus. It's an awkward fit, to be honest. Venus is in fall in Virgo, which is the astrologer's way of saying she's uncomfortable there and doesn't get listened to, so the pleasure-loving side of you has to come in by a side door. Usually it comes in through things done properly. The Eight of Pentacles, the Sun's slice, opens the sign bent over the workbench. The Ten, Mercury's slice, closes it thinking about family and what gets handed on. Yours is the one in the middle that gets to enjoy the result. Virgo's Major is The Hermit, so that's your Sun card, and this pip is the finer grain inside it.

You can tell within one sip whether the coffee at a new café is worth coming back for, and if it isn't, you just quietly never go back. A Sunday with nothing planned is one of your favourite things, as long as the flat is tidy first, and it usually means a long walk, a market, a good loaf of bread and nobody asking where you are. At a family dinner you're the one who notices the tablecloth has been ironed and says so, and the one who notices the gravy came out of a packet and doesn't. Virgo is ruled by Mercury, so there's a running commentary in your head about how everything could be done a little better. With Venus in fall here, enjoyment has to get past that commentary before you let yourself have it. When it does, when the bath is the right temperature and the book is good, you're about as content as anyone I know.

The gift people don't clock straight away is that you can make a small amount of money feel like plenty. Venus has to work indirectly in Virgo, so she works through care and editing, and you've learned to get real pleasure out of a few good things chosen well. Your first flat was probably nicer than friends' places that cost twice as much. Guests notice it too. There's a towel folded on the end of the bed, a glass of water on the side table, decent soap in the bathroom, and nobody saw you do any of it. When a friend moves out after a break-up with nothing but a suitcase, you're the one who turns up with three plates, a lamp and a proper knife, and by the end of the afternoon the place feels like somewhere a person lives.

The less obvious shadow is that you find it hard to enjoy anything you didn't earn yourself. A friend pays for dinner and you spend dessert working out how to pay them back. Someone gives you a spa voucher for your birthday and it sits in a drawer for eleven months, because a whole afternoon of being looked after, with nothing to show for it, feels faintly wrong. That's Venus in fall again. Pleasure doesn't get a hearing on its own terms, so you only let it in once it's been paid for with effort. There's a sharper edge to it as well. You can be a bit snobbish about other people's comforts, the takeaway, the reality telly, the cask wine, and people pick up on the little pause before you say it all looks lovely.

When things go wrong, a job that ends badly, a death in the family, months of being overlooked at work, the first thing you do is tidy. The drawers get sorted, the car gets cleaned, and you might buy one very good thing, a jumper or a heavy pan, as a private reassurance that life is still under control. It looks calm from outside. About a week later the Virgo side has turned on you, and you're going back over every choice you made, fairly sure you should have seen it coming. You pull away from people and tell them you're fine, you just need some time at home. The people close to you feel shut out of a house they're usually welcome in, which hurts them more than you'd guess. What actually helps is letting one person see the mess, and letting them cook for you even if they do it badly.

You're choosy and slow in love, and you'd sooner be on your own than with the wrong person, which some people mistake for coldness. What gets missed is how much of your affection comes out as small practical fixes. Venus doesn't speak easily in Virgo, so she speaks through the hands. You'll replace the broken zip on your partner's jacket without mentioning it. You remember they hate coriander and that their mother's birthday is in the same week as their work deadline. Saying the soft thing out loud is harder, and a partner who needs a lot of words can end up feeling unsure of you. The other side of it is that you want to be courted properly, a real restaurant, a planned day, and if the effort isn't there you notice, even if you never say so. Tell them what you'd like, plainly, a good week before the birthday.

At work you're the person whose finished thing looks easy, and nobody sees the eleven drafts. The Eight of Pentacles people are happy at the bench for good, and the Ten are building something for the next generation. Your slice wants the work to pay for a life you actually like, so you tend to end up self-employed, or senior enough to set your own hours, or in a field where taste is the product, editing, interiors, a small restaurant, garden design, a skin clinic, fine carpentry. You're good with money in a quiet way and you rarely get into debt. What costs you is pricing. Venus in fall makes it hard to put a proper value on your own work, so you undercharge for years and then feel resentful about it. Put your rates up every year, whether or not you feel ready.

At twenty this decan is often a bit uneasy. You've got expensive taste and not much money, and you can feel almost apologetic about wanting nice things when friends seem happy with whatever's going. A lot of people with this placement work very hard in their twenties and don't enjoy much of it. By the mid-thirties it tends to come together. There's a place of your own set up exactly how you like it, some savings, a routine that suits you, and the independence people admire in you has become real. That's often also when you notice you've built the whole garden and haven't invited anyone into it. The fifties usually bring a softening. People with this decan tend to get better at being given things, travel more, spend on pleasure without the long justification, and let their friends see how much they matter.

Once a month, spend a small fixed amount, say thirty dollars, on something purely for pleasure, with one rule. It can't be useful. No tools, no kitchen gear, no books you'll learn something from. A bunch of flowers, a very good peach, a ticket to a gig. Use it the same day, on your own if you like, and when the Virgo voice starts listing what the money could have gone on, let it finish the list and keep eating the peach.
